test: the home page names the parcel room and says what LockerLine is
what_should_happen: When the app opens on the home page, a small line names the building and its parcel room. The big heading reads "Forty-eight lockers." with "No notebook." on its second line, and a short paragraph says what couriers, residents and the caretaker do.
exact_words: Sunrise Heights · Tower A parcel room
Couriers get a locker in seconds, residents open it with a code that runs out, and the caretaker can see every locker, and every parcel's story, at a glance.

test: on an empty wall the counts read 48 lockers, 48 free right now and 0 holding parcels
what_should_happen: On a fresh start every locker is free. Once the home page has read the wall, its three counts read 48 lockers, 48 free right now and 0 holding parcels.

test: with parcels in D01 and D21 the counts read 48 lockers, 46 free right now and 2 holding parcels
what_should_happen: A small parcel sits in D01 and a medium one in D21 before the page opens. The counts come from the real wall, so they read 48 lockers, 46 free right now and 2 holding parcels.

reason: Whether the first small door in the picture looks like it is holding is a colour and a drawing; the picture is hidden from screen readers.

test: the picture shows the small doors D01 to D09 and the large doors D41 to D44, and nothing else
what_should_happen: The small picture of the wall shows exactly thirteen doors. They are the small doors D01 to D09 and the large doors D41 to D44, and no other door number appears on the page.

test: the picture is only a picture: clicking a door does nothing
what_should_happen: Clicking a door in the picture, small or large, does nothing. The address stays on the home page and no panel opens.

reason: Three rows of three small doors and two rows of two large ones is a layout, and each door's free or holding look is a colour; a pretend browser has neither.

test: before the wall answers the counts show 0 and the picture has no doors, then both fill in
what_should_happen: In the first moment, before the wall has answered, the counts show 0 and the picture has no doors at all. A moment later they fill in by themselves: 48 lockers, 48 free right now, and the doors appear.

test: under "Who are you today?" there is one card each for Farida, Imran and Mrs Rao
what_should_happen: Under "Who are you today?" a line says that each person sees their own screens. There are three cards, Farida the caretaker, Imran the courier and Mrs Rao the resident, each with its line about what the person does and "Continue as" with the name.
exact_words: Each person sees their own screens. Everything they do changes the same wall.
Runs the parcel room. Sees every locker, every parcel and the rules the wall follows.
Arrives with a bag of parcels. Asks for a locker by size and flat, and gets one.
Gets a code when a parcel arrives. Keys it in at the lobby and the locker opens.

test: clicking Farida's card goes to /caretaker/wall
what_should_happen: Each person card is one link. Clicking Farida's card takes the address to /caretaker/wall.

test: clicking Imran's card goes to /courier
what_should_happen: Each person card is one link. Clicking Imran's card takes the address to /courier.

test: clicking Mrs Rao's card goes to /resident
what_should_happen: Each person card is one link. Clicking Mrs Rao's card takes the address to /resident.

test: on the home page the header has the logo and no ← button or person button
what_should_happen: On the home page the header shows only the LockerLine logo with "Sunrise Heights · Tower A" beside it. There is no ← button and no person button, because nobody has been chosen yet.

test: the ← button (Back to the home page) on a person's page goes home
what_should_happen: On a person's page, such as the courier's, the header has a ← button named "Back to the home page". Clicking it takes the address back to the home page.

test: the logo on a person's page goes home
what_should_happen: The LockerLine logo is a link home on every page. Clicking it on the wall takes the address back to the home page.

test: the person button shows Farida, Imran or the Rao family with their role and initial
what_should_happen: The person button in the header says whose screens these are. On the wall it shows F, Farida and Caretaker, and on the courier's page I, Imran and Courier. On the resident's page it shows R, "Rao family" and "Resident · Flat 302".

reason: The colour of each person's initial circle is only visible in a real browser.

test: the person button opens "View the parcel room as" with Farida, Imran and the Rao family
what_should_happen: Clicking the person button on the wall opens a menu headed "View the parcel room as". It has exactly three options: Farida (Caretaker), Imran (Courier) and Rao family (Resident · Flat 302).

reason: The tick beside Farida is a drawing that screen readers skip, so only a real browser shows it.

test: choosing Imran closes the menu and opens /courier with Imran in the header
what_should_happen: With the person menu open, choosing Imran closes the menu. The address becomes /courier and the person button now shows Imran.

test: pointing at the resident option opens "Which resident are you?" with the 16 flats, floor by floor
what_should_happen: Pointing at the resident option opens a panel headed "Which resident are you?" with Floor 1 to Floor 4. It lists the building's 16 flats, from 101 Iyer to 404 Jain, and only flat 302 is marked as the current one.

test: the resident option opens the flats with Enter, as a click does
what_should_happen: The resident option also opens the flats when it is used like a button, with a click or with Enter from the keyboard. Tabbing to it and pressing Enter shows "Which resident are you?" and the 16 flats.

test: pointing at the resident option and then clicking it keeps the flats open
what_should_happen: With a mouse, the flats open as soon as the pointer is on the resident option. Clicking the option then must keep them open, so the resident can go on to choose a flat. A click that shuts them again is a mistake.

reason: That the flats open beside the menu, in rows of four, and that 302 looks dark with a tick, are layout and colour.

test: choosing 304 Chawla closes the menu and makes the app the Chawla family's on /resident
what_should_happen: Choosing flat 304 Chawla in the flats panel closes the menu and goes to /resident. The title row says "Flat 304" and "Hello, Chawla family", and the person button shows "Chawla family" with "Resident · Flat 304".

test: a flat with a parcel waiting carries a dot, and the foot of the flats explains it
what_should_happen: A parcel waits for flat 302 before the page opens. In the flats panel, 302 carries a dot named "A parcel is waiting" while 304 has none, and the foot of the panel explains the dot with the same words.

test: Esc closes the person menu and nothing changes
what_should_happen: With the person menu open on the wall, pressing Esc closes it. The page stays on the wall and Farida is still the person in the header.

test: a click outside the person menu closes it and nothing changes
what_should_happen: With the person menu open, clicking somewhere else on the page closes it. The page stays on the wall and Farida is still the person in the header.

test: clicking the person button again closes the menu and nothing changes
what_should_happen: The person button opens the menu and a second click on it closes the menu again. The page stays where it was.

test: after choosing flat 304, a refresh makes the app the Rao family of flat 302 again
what_should_happen: The chosen flat is kept only while the page is open. After choosing flat 304 and refreshing the page, the header shows the Rao family again and the page says "Hello, Rao family".

test: the wall's title row reads "Tower A parcel room" and "The wall", with The wall tab filled
what_should_happen: The wall's title row shows the small line "Tower A parcel room" and the heading "The wall". It has two tabs, "The wall" and "Parcels", and "The wall" is marked as the page you are on.

reason: The current tab being filled in Farida's colour is a colour.

test: the Parcels tab opens /caretaker/parcels, whose title row reads "Every drop, code and opening" and "Parcels"
what_should_happen: Clicking the Parcels tab on the wall goes to /caretaker/parcels. Its title row shows "Every drop, code and opening" and the heading "Parcels", and now the Parcels tab is the one marked as current.

test: with three lockers holding parcels the Parcels tab carries a badge with 3
what_should_happen: Three parcels sit in lockers before the wall opens. The Parcels tab carries a small badge with the number 3.

test: with no locker holding anything the Parcels tab has no badge
what_should_happen: On a fresh start no locker holds anything. The Parcels tab then reads just "Parcels", with no badge and no 0.

test: the courier's title row reads "Drop-off · Tower A" and "Get a locker", with no tabs
what_should_happen: Imran's page has the small line "Drop-off · Tower A" and the heading "Get a locker". The courier has only one page, so there are no tabs.

test: the resident with nothing waiting sees "Flat 302" and "Hello, Rao family", with no tabs
what_should_happen: With nothing waiting for flat 302, the resident's title row shows "Flat 302" and "Hello, Rao family". There are no tabs, because My parcels alone is not a choice.

test: with two parcels waiting the resident has the tabs My parcels and Collect, and Collect carries a badge with 2
what_should_happen: Two parcels wait for flat 302 before the page opens. The resident's title row then has two tabs, "My parcels" and "Collect", and Collect carries a badge with the number 2.

test: on /resident/collect with nothing waiting the title row reads "Lobby keypad" and "Collect a parcel", with both tabs
what_should_happen: On the Collect page the title row shows "Lobby keypad" and the heading "Collect a parcel". Even with nothing waiting both tabs show, Collect marked as current, so the resident can go back to My parcels.

test: /caretaker leads to /caretaker/wall
what_should_happen: Typing the short address /caretaker opens the wall. The address becomes /caretaker/wall and the heading reads "The wall".

test: /caretaker/parcels/P001 leads to /caretaker/parcels
what_should_happen: Typing an old parcel address such as /caretaker/parcels/P001 lands on the Parcels page. The address becomes /caretaker/parcels and the heading reads "Parcels".

test: an address the app does not have, such as /lobby, leads to the home page
what_should_happen: Typing an address the app does not have, such as /lobby, lands on the home page. The address becomes / and the header has only the logo.

reason: The app's own slim scroll bar, dragging it and clicking its track need a real page height and a real mouse; a pretend browser has no layout.
Whether a page fits in the window depends on real heights, which a pretend browser does not measure.

test: on an empty wall the five count cards read 48, 48, 0, "—" and 0 with their notes
what_should_happen: On a fresh start every locker is free. The five count cards read "Total lockers" 48 with "20 small · 20 medium · 8 large", "Free lockers" 48 with "ready for a parcel", "Holding parcels" 0 with "nothing dropped yet", "Longest wait" "—" with "dwell time", and "Codes expired" 0 with "all codes still valid".

test: the wall shows three banks in number order: Small D01 to D20, Medium D21 to D40, Large D41 to D48, all free
what_should_happen: The wall has three banks, read out as Small lockers, Medium lockers and Large lockers, in that order. Small holds D01 to D20 and reads "20/20 free", Medium holds D21 to D40 with "20/20 free", and Large holds D41 to D48 with "8/8 free", every bank in number order.

reason: Each door's light showing free is a colour.

test: a parcel that has waited 3h 30m in D21 shows on its door and in the count cards
what_should_happen: A medium parcel went into D21 three and a half hours before the wall opens. Door D21 reads "3h 30m", the Medium bank reads "19/20 free", and the cards read "Holding parcels" 1 with "waiting for residents", "Free lockers" 47 and "Longest wait" "3h 30m".

reason: The parcel drawn inside D21 and its light showing holding are a drawing and a colour.

test: waits of 5 minutes, 3 hours 30 minutes and 1 day 20 hours read "5m", "3h 30m" and "1d 20h", the longest in the card
what_should_happen: Three parcels have waited 5 minutes, 3 hours 30 minutes and 1 day 20 hours. Their doors read "5m", "3h 30m" and "1d 20h", and "Longest wait" reads "1d 20h".

test: a parcel still in its locker after its 48-hour free window counts in "Codes expired"
what_should_happen: One parcel has sat in its locker for just over 48 hours, past its code's free window, while another went in more recently. The "Codes expired" card reads 1 with "parcels past their free window".

reason: The card standing out as a warning is a colour.

test: the legend under the wall shows "Free" and "Holding a parcel"
what_should_happen: Under the wall a legend explains the two states. It reads "Free" and "Holding a parcel".

reason: The colour beside each word of the legend can only be seen in a real browser.

test: before the wall is read no count cards and no doors show, then they appear
what_should_happen: In the first moment, before the wall has answered, there are no count cards and no doors, not even zeros. As soon as the wall is read the cards appear with "Total lockers" 48 and all 48 doors show.

test: with the wall left open for a minute, D21's waiting time and "Longest wait" grow by themselves
what_should_happen: D21 has held a parcel for 3h 30m when the wall opens. After a minute with the page left open, without a reload, D21 and "Longest wait" no longer read "3h 30m" but a minute more.
